versions.changelog: v1.8.3.35: The player button no longer needs write access to Jellyfin's web folder. The plugin adds its script to index.html as Jellyfin serves the page, so Windows installs (NetworkService), the Debian package, snaps and read-only containers get the button in every browser tab. Behind a Jellyfin base URL, the Lanczos, Anime4K and WebGPU real-time engines load again. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.34: Real-time upscaling starts again in the web client. Since v1.8.3.31 it refused every video with "Video color metadata unavailable", because Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer put the playing item in the page address; the player now reads the item from the video's stream or the web client's playback request and checks the version that plays. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.33: Redesigned in-player menu and settings page. SDR videos (DVD/SD rips, untagged 10-bit) are no longer refused as HDR in real time or in library jobs; HDR batch output keeps the model's detail; Server AI hides stale frames during outages and falls back to Lanczos when the server cannot keep up. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.32: Native Jellyfin 12 build on .NET 10, aligned plugin/test dependencies, updated CI and ABI-aware release validation. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.31: Remove the image-action rate limit from playback frames/chunks; forward busy/error responses and Retry-After; serialize player captures with abortable requests and backoff; guard driver upscaling and object masking; enforce measured Auto-mode performance; reject invalid model categories and unsupported HDR; fail library jobs on AI errors without local resize/original-frame substitution; enforce nonempty passing TRX and publish-only runtime packaging. Target-server acceptance was explicitly waived by the owner; GPU, live-player and HDR target-hardware behavior remain unverified.

v1.8.3.30: notifications stack instead of piling up - issue #77, 'if you hit a toggle in quick succession, the notifications at the lower right side of the screen will simply pile on top of each other'. They did, literally: every notification was its own position:fixed element anchored to the same corner, so two of them resolved to the identical coordinates and the second covered the first. Measured in a browser against the real CSS - three toasts all reported top 1185 / bottom 1226; after the fix 1185, 1136, 1087 with no overlap. They are flow children of one fixed host now and the host does the stacking, column-reverse so the newest sits nearest the corner. Two things beyond the literal report, both aimed at what 'quick succession' actually produces: a repeated toggle emits the SAME text over and over, so an identical message already on screen has its timer restarted instead of being cloned (firing 'Settings saved!' five times leaves one), and the stack is capped at four so holding a control down cannot fill the viewport. THE PLUGIN HAD THREE COPIES of this code, each with the same defect - the config page (reported), the player overlay and the quick menu - and all three are fixed, because patching only the reported surface is how the same bug gets filed twice. sidebar-upscaler.js was already correct (it defers to Jellyfin's own toast module) and a test now keeps it that way. Verified by measurement, not by reading: a browser harness built from the real CSS and the real showToast confirmed stacking, de-duplication and the cap, and re-applying the old position:fixed rule reproduced the exact overlap from the screenshot. Eleven regression tests; five reintroduced defects are each caught. 375 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.29: the error message now says what went wrong. Testing v1.8.3.28 live showed the last piece of the same problem - a failed Load Detection Model printed one generic sentence regardless of cause, because the handler read err.responseText (an XHR field) while Jellyfin 10.11's client is fetch-based. Checked against the running server rather than assumed: the rejection is [object Response], err.text IS a function, err.responseText does not exist, status 404 - so JSON.parse(undefined) threw on every failure and the fallback was the only thing anyone saw, while the body carried exactly what was needed ('... is not on disk. Import or upload a detection model first'). That reaches the status line now. The same run confirmed the v1.8.3.28 modelName parameter end to end: the service named the id that was passed, not the saved one. The old fallback also advised saving the settings first, which stopped being true in v1.8.3.28 when the button began saving them itself. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.28: the two object-masking UI bugs reported in discussion #11, where the feature itself is confirmed working - Ultralytics YOLO exports load (YOLO26n fastest in the reporter's testing), boxes land where they should, 5-10 fps at low quality on a Ryzen 5 7600 through docker7-cpu. 'THE STATUS WOULD OFTEN STICK ON A PREVIOUS MODEL NAME' - because it was telling the truth: the button POSTed nothing and the endpoint read only the SAVED config, so a newly typed id loaded the PREVIOUS model and the status correctly named that one. A comment in the UI described this exact trap and guarded only against an empty field; documenting a bug is not fixing it. The endpoint takes a modelName parameter now, the button sends what is on screen, and the saved value stays as the fallback for scripts. 'IT SEEMED TO IGNORE THE CONFIDENCE VALUES I PUT IN' - it did. step=0.05 makes a type=number input report value === '' for entries the browser rejects, and floating point puts ordinary values off that grid: (0.6-0.05)/0.05 evaluates to 10.999999999999998, so 0.6 was rejected. The save path skipped empty strings, which normally means 'left blank' but here meant 'the browser disliked it', so the number vanished without a word. Now step=any, parsed and clamped, and the stored value written back into the field. Both share a root cause: an action button sits next to fields that were not persisted until the global Save, so Load Detection Model now saves the card first - which also stops values reverting when you navigate away and back. Four regression tests, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.27: three defects a live server showed that no unit test could. EVERY TRANSLATED STRING HAS BEEN FALLING BACK TO ITS KEY on every install since the i18n work landed - strings.en.json is declared as an EmbeddedResource, MSBuild lists it as one, and it was not in the DLL, because MSBuild reads the '.en.' in the file name as a CULTURE TAG and compiles it into a satellite assembly the release ZIP does not ship. Jellyfin logged 'Failed to get resource' on every config-page load. The test guarding it asserted that the .csproj MENTIONED the file, which it always did; it now reads the built assembly's manifest resource names, and removing the fix fails it. /hardware-info REPORTED THREE THINGS IT NEVER CHECKED: GpuAvailable returned the HardwareAcceleration config toggle (default on), so a CPU-only server was told it had a GPU while /gpu-verify on the same box reported no devices at all; FFmpegAvailable was the literal true and OnnxRuntime the literal 'Available'. All three are observations now, null means 'not asked yet' rather than 'no', and what the user requested is a separate field. THE FRAME PROXIES THREW AWAY THE DIAGNOSIS: after a container restart the service answers {'detail': 'No model loaded'} and both proxies replaced it with 'Frame upscaling failed'; confirmed that was all it was by loading fsrcnn-x2 and getting 200 at 4.7 fps / 214 ms per frame at 480x270 on a CPU-only box. Also two documentation errors found the same way: GET /Upscaler/health is listed and does not exist (only health/detailed), and benchmark-frame is a GET, not a POST. 360 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.26: the plugin downloads the detector itself - tiny-yolov3 is a catalog entry now, so the Models tab fetches and verifies it exactly like an upscaler instead of asking you to bring your own. That became possible only once the pin could be VERIFIED rather than asserted: the file was downloaded, its sha384 checked against the OpenVINO model zoo's own model.yml, and the catalog's sha256 computed from those exact bytes. A REAL MODEL FOUND A REAL BUG: loading the actual tiny-yolov3 on a live server reported input_size 640, because the export declares its spatial dims as ('N', 3, None, None) - nothing in the file says 416 - so the loader used the generic fallback while the anchors are trained for 416. The code was right and the result was wrong; every synthetic test model declares a fixed size, so no test could reach that path. The catalog carries net_size 416 and the loader prefers it. Also two bugs in the catalog sync script, found by running it: it EXECUTED main.py to read the model list (needing fastapi, OpenCV and ONNX Runtime) and had failed outright since v1.8.3.23 with 'attempted relative import' after `from . import object_mask` was added - it parses with ast now; and it would have collapsed the pretty-printed catalog onto one line, because PowerShell captures output as an array and Out-File -NoNewline joins array elements with no separator. 356 C# + 166 Python green.

v1.8.3.25: detection models could not be imported AT ALL - reported in discussion #11 and it was my bug. The import gate hard-required a 4D output, so every detection model was rejected with 'Expected 4D output (N, C, H, W), got shape [1, None, 4]' - the boxes tensor of exactly the yolo-v3-tiny export object masking was built for. v1.8.3.24 could load a detector and mask with it, and there was no way to get one in; every test for that release started from a model already sitting in the models directory, so none walked the path a user walks. The fix is a shared gate rather than an override switch: the importer classifies the model - 4D in and 4D out is an upscaler, otherwise it asks object_mask.plan_for, the SAME function that decides how to drive it at load time. A model that imports is a model that loads; a laxer separate check would only move the rejection to a later step, which is worse because by then the user believes it is installed. An imported detector registers as object-detection with no scale factor, so it stays out of the upscaler dropdowns and auto-mode cannot pick it for a video, and the category survives a container restart. A model that is neither is refused with BOTH readings explained. Six tests cover import to load to mask as one path; against the old gate five of them fail with the reporter's exact message. NOTE: the fix lives in the AI service - update the Docker image too. 354 C# + 166 Python tests green. Also fixes two shutdown bugs found by installing this build on a real server: VideoProcessor released the processing permit as the first statement of its finally block, so on shutdown ObjectDisposedException skipped the rest of the cleanup and a clean stop was logged as a processing failure; and a progress update to an already disposed SessionManager logged a warning with a stack trace on every shutdown with a running job. 356 C# tests green.

v1.8.3.24: object masking now runs DURING PLAYBACK - the part of discussion #11 that v1.8.3.23 did not deliver. That release shipped the masking as a service endpoint nothing called, while the request was for a real-time filter; the user could already produce the result externally, live during playback was the whole point. The player's capture loop already existed for server-side upscaling - it pulls frames off the video element and draws the result onto an overlay - and masking simply had nowhere to send them. Enable it in Settings (classes, box or blur, padding, confidence) plus an admin-gated button that loads the detector, or toggle it live in the player menu under Auto - Cover objects. It REPLACES real-time upscaling while running: upscaling and detecting is two full inference passes per frame, which no realistic server sustains at playback rate, and both surfaces say so rather than letting you discover it as stutter. Batch upscaling is untouched. Padding defaults to 12px because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with the plugin - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin. TESTS THAT CAN ACTUALLY FAIL: mutation testing on v1.8.3.23 found two guards asserting text rather than behaviour - the neighbouring-directory bypass could be fully reintroduced with the suite green (the test asserted the source contained 'rootWithSep', which the bypass leaves in place), and the critical path check was guarded by counting occurrences of IsInsideMediaLibrary( so making the call unreachable kept both the count and the green suite. Both are exercised now: the containment rule is a tested function and ProcessVideo is called with a mocked library manager. The same pass deleted a state field written but never read, and the AI service's masking endpoints are now driven end to end by real synthesised ONNX models, one per detector family. Also: a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md the contributing page had been linking to while the file did not exist, and every site page showed the current version in the topbar and v1.8.3.13 in the footer - eleven releases stale, because the sync script and the audit both only looked at the topbar. The class list is URL-encoded and confidence formatted invariantly, so 'dog&mode=blur' cannot become a second query parameter and de-DE cannot send 0,35. 354 C# + 160 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.23: object masking, the answer to discussion #11 - a user's dog reacts to dogs and cats on TV and asked for ffmpeg's dnn_detect + drawbox via a custom -vf chain. That cannot work here: jellyfin-ffmpeg's build carries 46 --enable-* flags and no DNN backend at all (no libopenvino/libtensorflow/libtorch, the string 'dnn' does not appear in it), so those filters are absent from the ffmpeg Jellyfin ships whatever the plugin passes. Arbitrary -vf would also be a hole rather than a feature - ffmpeg filter syntax includes movie= and subtitles=, which read files, handing every authenticated user the same primitive v1.8.3.22 just closed on POST /process. So it is done in the AI service, which already loads ONNX models per frame: POST /models/load-detector loads a detector alongside the upscaler rather than instead of it, and POST /detect-mask covers detections with a filled box or a blur, by COCO class or the 'animals' group, with padding because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with it - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin and inventing one would break exactly the guarantee the importer provides, so users bring their own through the existing upload/import path. The decoder handles the v3/v5/v7 and v8/v9 layouts and refuses anything else, because a misread tensor does not throw, it paints boxes over the wrong part of the picture. Also: the face-restore preview proxy read request bodies into the Jellyfin heap unbounded and is now capped at 32 MB, and a static check over the whole AI service asserts every global name its code references exists - written because the detector loader called a helper this service has never had, which Python resolves at call time, so the module imported cleanly and the endpoint would have raised NameError the first time anyone used it. 321 C# + 140 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.22: code-review fixes - one critical and nine confirmed high findings, each re-verified against the code first. SECURITY: POST /process accepted any path on the server (the controller carries only [Authorize] and, unlike its two siblings, had no media-library allowlist) - with ffmpeg's -y an arbitrary-overwrite primitive, plus a file-existence oracle; there is one shared separator-safe allowlist now and neither job entry point overwrites an existing file. AUTO MODE WAS NEVER RUNNING IN BATCH: Model defaulted to realesrgan-x4 while the nightly scan gates on 'auto enabled and model empty or auto', so that gate was always false and every batch run skipped the hardware cap and 8K guard while the dashboard displayed Auto - the default is empty now and the dropdown finally offers Auto. LOCALE: fps= and both -ss values used the current culture, so on de-DE/fr-FR 23.976 became fps=23,976 and a comma is the ffmpeg filter separator - every frame-by-frame job on those servers failed. QUEUE: two permit leaks plus an empty-queue branch that handed the surplus back = 100% of a core after any cancel. Three silent misreports fixed: a Lanczos fallback stored as an AI result (which made the scan filter skip that image forever), an HDR URL that 404'd on a trailing slash while reporting success, and expired cache entries orphaning multi-GB files. And cleanup-dockerhub-tags would have deleted all 71 current tags and re-pointed :latest to a v1.7.8 image - the version is derived from meta.json now. 14 regression guards; 315 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.21: maintainability groundwork - two structural packages, nothing user-facing. model_import.py is a verbatim extraction of the OpenModelDB import and pth->ONNX conversion block from main.py (6808 -> 6627 lines): byte-identical function bodies, no route moved, the endpoints keep their decorators. Three test monkeypatch targets moved with it, and one had been passing for the wrong reason. i18n groundwork makes English a SOURCE language read from Configuration/strings.en.json via a small t() helper - adding a locale is copying the file, translating values and one line of code. Nothing was translated; this phase proves the structure. The scope was cut deliberately: a full extraction is ~485 strings with no user-visible benefit until a translation exists, and the existing UI guard checks element ids rather than text, so a botched sweep would ship silently. 58 keys are migrated - the activity strip and auto-mode texts, all new or rewritten in v1.8.3.20. A missing key renders as the key name rather than an empty string, and t() takes a fallback so the first paint never flashes key names. docs/I18N.md records the numbers and how to continue. 300 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.20: honesty, visibility, reproducibility - five packages, no features. The UI promised 'AI picks model + filter per video' and the code half-kept it: auto stopped overwriting a chosen preset in v1.8.3.14 but still wrote its own whenever the field was empty, so the first playback quietly decided your look. Auto now never writes a filter at all - it offers one in the player's Auto tab and the sidebar with an Apply button, and only when its opinion differs from yours. The activity strip is one line stating phase, frame x of y, model with the auto reason, fps and ETA; those numbers were computed every frame and discarded, and the old 'N jobs completed' counted a list that never contains completed jobs. docs/ENDPOINT-AUDIT.md reports all 66 routes against their real callers (20 unreferenced, grouped by what they are - including six Processing Queue endpoints the settings page configures but no UI ever calls). /Upscaler/hardware-benchmark retires the misleading /Upscaler/recommendations name, which stays as a deprecated alias with an identical payload. Reproducible builds finally are: lock files existed since v1.8.3.13 and no image installed one; five variants now install hash-pinned locks with --require-hashes, and intel and nvidia produced their first lock ever. The Python suite had been red since v1.8.3.14 and shipped over six releases because pytest was not a gate - it is now, and the download path plus the SSRF gate have real coverage. 293 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.19: the Auto tab no longer states a default as a fact. Browser-testing the new tab against the live server caught it reporting 'RUNNING NOW / nomosuni-compact-x2 / HD content in real time' on a page where no video was playing: with no video element the resolver is handed 0x0, falls through to its HD branch, and the pane presented that fallback as a decision about the file in front of you - while also printing the literal string 'unknown output size' as though it were data. Three headings now, matched to what is actually known: 'Running now' when a video is playing and auto is on, 'Auto would pick' when auto is off, and 'Default pick - start playback for this file' when there are no dimensions to decide from. In that last state the output size and the resolution-derived reason are omitted rather than printed, because both would be fabricated; the model, its scale and the signals list stay, because 'Resolution: unknown' is true and useful. Verified in a real browser against the deployed plugin: Auto leads the tab bar, all four switches render their config state, and toggling face restoration flipped EnableFaceRestore, persisted it and re-rendered the pane. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.18: Auto mode gets its own tab in the player. Auto has been the default since v1.8.3.12, but the in-player panel only ever asked the Custom-mode questions - pick a model, pick a filter - and could not answer the one that matters while a video is running: what did auto decide for THIS file, and how do I turn it off without leaving the player. The panel now leads with an Auto tab showing the model, its scale, the resulting output size, the reason, the signals it looked at and any substitution warning, plus live switches for auto mode, video filters, face restoration and real-time upscaling - each takes effect immediately, and 'Re-apply to this video' re-runs the decision against the running upscaler. The filter row states what is true: auto suggests a look and never overwrites a preset you chose. Docs caught up too: site/configuration.html described auto-selection with models that are not in the catalog (hat-x4, swinir-m-x4, realesrgan-x4plus) and a genre mapping the resolver never had; it now carries the real decision table plus the hardware-budget and scale-ceiling filters. README gains an Auto Mode section. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.17: 4K sources are cleaned up, not enlarged. TargetScaleFor has answered 1x for sources that are already 4K since v1.8.3.14, but nothing acted on it - only the substitution filter read it and no branch ever produced a 1x pick, so a 4K source still went to 7680x4320. There is now an explicit branch ahead of the multi-frame and anime paths: a 4K source gets a 1x restoration model that removes compression artefacts at the original size. Second cause: the scale parser knew only the 'x<N>' order (realesrgan-x4) and not the '<N>x' order used by the 1x restoration models (dejpg-realplksr-1x) and by every OpenModelDB import (omdb-4x-nomos8k-atd), so every 1x model reported unknown scale; both are parsed now, end-anchored first so realesrgan-x4-256 still means 4x. The overshoot test theory now includes 4K - leaving it out is what hid this - and states the honest invariant: exceeding the target factor must be a reported substitution carrying a reason. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.16: a substitution must not overshoot the target size. The quality ladder added in v1.8.3.15 picked by weight alone, so a branch that had deliberately chosen a 2x model for 1080p was handed clearreality-x4 - cheap, Light and 4x - producing 7680x4320 with the branch's own reason text ('a 4x pass would target 8K for no visible gain') printed next to it; a 4K source reached 15360x8640. A substitute now has to fit the hardware AND stay within the resolution's target factor, and when nothing satisfies both, the affordable candidate with the smallest scale wins so the overshoot is as small as available. Branch fallbacks are still tried before the ladder, and an id that encodes no scale is not rejected because unknown is not the same as too big. SD keeps its full 4x restore. 270 tests green, including a theory across weak-cpu/strong-cpu/igpu x 720p/1080p x live-action/anime asserting no pick ever exceeds its target factor.

v1.8.3.15: three defects that only a real machine could show, found deploying v1.8.3.14 to a CPU-only server. PreferredAnimeModel shipped with a default of anime-compact-x4, and the resolver cannot tell a shipped default from a deliberate user choice - which is exempt from the hardware budget and the scale logic by design - so EVERY anime decision skipped both and a CPU-only box got a 4x model on 1080p (7680x4320); the default is now empty like its live-action counterpart (saved values are kept: set Preferred Anime Model back to Auto if you never chose one deliberately). The v1.8.3.14 8K fix only covered live action - anime batch still targeted 8K on 1080p. And the budget fallback only walked a branch's own candidates, none of which contain a light model, so on a weak CPU every live-action job collapsed to the last-resort fsrcnn-x2 while clearreality-x4 is equally cheap, does 4x and is ~32x faster than realesrgan-x4 per CPU tile; there is now a quality ladder within each weight class. Reasons describe the material instead of naming a model, so a reason can no longer advertise something that was substituted away. 266 tests green.

v1.8.3.14: Auto mode respects your hardware, and tells the truth about scale. The content heuristic and the AI service's hardware advisor were two separate recommenders that never spoke to each other, so a CPU-only NAS could be handed a full restoration net; the hardware class is now cached and an over-budget pick falls back with a stated reason (an unknown class caps nothing, and a model you picked yourself is never overridden). The service ignores the requested scale and uses the model's native factor, so the library scan logged scale=2x while auto ran a 4x model - a 1080p batch job silently produced 8K frames; the real factor is now read from the model, reported by the API, used by the job, and a 1080p batch no longer defaults to 4x. Every downloadable catalog model gets a Get button (27 of them had none) with real byte progress, and 'Not DL' is split into 'Not downloaded' vs 'Self-host only'. Pause/Resume/Cancel added to the dashboard activity strip. Auto mode no longer overwrites a filter preset you chose. Batch runs log their model reasoning at Information instead of Debug. Stray scrollbar next to the tab row removed. 262 tests green.

Build side: APP_VERSION defaults removed from all 7 Dockerfiles (six said 1.8.2, one 1.8.3.8 - the service reported a wrong version) with a release-guard assert, new weekly lock workflow resolving each Python layer inside its real base image, and CI now builds five image variants per push instead of one. New docs/DOCKER-IMAGES.md with real image sizes and the AMD stack CVE + exit trigger. Tests: xUnit 199, pytest 112.

New catalog fields license/attribution/sha256; the service now VERIFIES the sha256 before a downloaded model is activated. Details: docs/MODEL-EVAL-2026-07.md. v1.8.3.2: Remove dead SSH remote-transcoding (Issue #73). The docker7 image dropped sshd long ago (non-root appuser hardening), but the plugin still shipped SSH remote-transcoding config + UI, a /Upscaler/ssh/test endpoint that shelled out to ssh, and an FFmpeg-wrapper-script installer (/Upscaler/wrapper/*). Plugin-only; existing docker7 images unaffected. Tests: xUnit 164, build clean.

v1.8.3.1: Cancel-fix (plugin-only, no Docker change). jobs/{id}/cancel reported success but never stopped a running job - VideoProcessor.ProcessVideoAsync created a per-job CancellationTokenSource (the token CancelJob cancels) but passed the bare caller token to the processing pipeline instead of the job's linked cts.Token, so cancellation never reached extraction/upscaling. The semaphore wait, model-load and the method executor now all receive cts.Token (still linked to the caller token), so Cancel stops the job promptly. Pre-existing across all processing methods. Tests: xUnit 164, build clean.

v1.8.3: Opt-in pipeline parallelism (plugin-only, no Docker change). New experimental setting 'Pipeline parallelism' (default OFF) overlaps frame extraction with upscaling instead of running them strictly back-to-back: while ffmpeg is still extracting later frames, already-extracted frames are upscaled concurrently. Built on a thread-safe FrameStreamCoordinator that hands a frame to the upscaler only once a successor frame proves it was fully written, and drops the unproven highest frame if extraction fails, so the output frame-count and ordering are identical to the sequential path. Default behaviour is unchanged; the overlap runs only when the box is ticked. Works with the existing docker7 AI-service images (no rebuild needed). Tests: xUnit 164 (incl. FrameStreamCoordinator COMPLETE-vs-FAILED asymmetry + terminal-first-wins), dotnet build clean.

v1.8.2: Quality + hardening pass. (1) Denoise-before-encode prefilter (hqdn3d/nlmeans) - a dedicated source-clean pass run BEFORE upscaling/encoding, independent of the camera-style filters (cleaner input -> better SR + smaller re-encode). (2) VMAF quality scoring - admin-only POST /Upscaler/vmaf scores an upscaled/distorted file against a reference via ffmpeg+libvmaf (501 if the build lacks libvmaf). (3) Second frame-interpolation architecture beside RIFE: the engine is now input-signature-adaptive (RIFE 1/2-input, IFRNet 3-input, CAIN 2-input); IFRNet+CAIN added as experimental self-host. (4) MultiFrame extraction now reports live progress (previously only FrameByFrame/Batch). (5) Decoupled model download: POST /models/download-async + GET /models/download-status/{id} run big downloads in the background so they no longer trip client/proxy timeouts. (6) Supply-chain: all 6 Docker base images pinned by @sha256 digest + pip-audit CVE sweep (0 known). (7) New client-VSR-vs-server hardware doc chapter + verified FrameStreamCoordinator. Needs AI service image >= v1.8.2 (docker7) for /vmaf, /recommend and async download. Tests: pytest 73, xUnit 159, dotnet build clean.

v1.8.1: Live filter fix + hardware-aware model recommendation. (1) In-player live filters (presets/sliders) had no visible effect while realtime client-side upscaling (Anime4K/WebGL/WebGPU) was active - the upscaler renders to a canvas overlay that covered the filtered <video>, so the CSS filter sat on a hidden element; it is now applied to the visible canvas too. (2) New GET /recommend (service) and GET /Upscaler/recommend (plugin, admin) pick a model + scale the detected hardware can actually run (weak CPU -> fsrcnn-x2 @2x, dedicated GPU -> realesrgan-x4), avoiding the wrong-model-on-weak-hardware wall. The recommend endpoint needs the AI service image >= v1.8.1 (docker7). Tests: pytest 50, xUnit 137, dotnet build clean.

v1.8.0: Managed API tokens. The service keeps them in a persistent /app/config volume and validates X-Api-Token against the env API_TOKEN (now a non-revocable bootstrap) OR any active managed token - both timing-safe, expiry checked lazily (no background sweep). New endpoints: service /auth/tokens (GET/POST/DELETE), plugin /Upscaler/tokens (admin-only proxy). Requires the AI service image >= v1.8.0 (docker7) so /auth/tokens exists. Tests: pytest 22, build clean.

Tests 137/137.

The UI error parsers now read detail||error||message so the real cause is shown instead of a generic 'Load failed'. New DI test asserts the named-client timeouts (120/300/570) so a typo cannot silently fall back to the 100s default. Tests 137/137.

v1.7.7: Docker Self-Verification Hardening. Structural completion of the Intel-Arc saga (#45/#66/#67/#69). A dedicated docker-ai-service deep-analysis found no acute bugs left but the MISSING VERIFICATION LAYER that let the whole saga's bug class slip through: no Dockerfile checked at build time whether its expected ONNX provider was actually installed. That gap shipped the v1.7.5 Intel bug (plain onnxruntime built fine, no OpenVINO EP, ran on CPU while dashboard showed GPU). FIX: (1) Dockerfile (NVIDIA) + Dockerfile.intel now assert CUDAExecutionProvider / OpenVINOExecutionProvider after pip install - HARD-FAIL (exit 1) if missing, so a broken GPU image cannot be published. (2) Dockerfile.amd gets a warn-only assert (exit 0, since CPU is a valid AMD fallback when ROCm wheels are yanked) that makes the silent CPU fallback visible in the build log. (3) entrypoint.sh detect_backend() now knows WSL2 /dev/dxg so the startup banner no longer falsely says 'Backend: cpu' on WSL2 setups where main.py correctly detects the GPU. C# Plugin DLL bit-identical to v1.7.6 - all changes in docker-ai-service. Tests 123/123 unchanged. v1.7.x configs bit-compatible.

v1.7.6: Intel OpenVINO Provider Hotfix. Closes the last open Point of issue #69 (Intel Arc GPU detected but inference ran on CPU). Verified empirically via Laurent (FrRene06)'s /gpu-verify output: onnx_providers showed only [AzureExecutionProvider, CPUExecutionProvider] - no OpenVINOExecutionProvider at all. Root cause: requirements-intel.txt had a wrong comment claiming onnxruntime-openvino was deprecated and that plain onnxruntime + system OpenVINO would work; in reality, plain onnxruntime from PyPI does NOT bundle the OpenVINOExecutionProvider, even with system OpenVINO present in the base image. Fix: single-line swap onnxruntime -> onnxruntime-openvino in requirements-intel.txt. After Docker Hub rebuild + container restart, /gpu-verify shows OpenVINOExecutionProvider as active provider and Intel GPU is actually used for inference. v1.6.1.16: Hotfix for issue #64 — LibraryUpscaleScanTask was failing on every item with two related cold-start errors ("File not found: ffprobe" → then after partial fix "Cannot start process because a file name has not been provided"). Root cause: THREE singletons (VideoAnalyzer, VideoFrameProcessor, ProcessingMethodExecutor) all captured empty ffmpeg/ffprobe path strings at plugin construction time, before Jellyfin's MediaEncoder finished resolving /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/{ffmpeg,ffprobe}. Fix: new EnsureFFmpegReady() in VideoProcessor re-resolves EncoderPath/ProbePath on demand, reconfigures FFMpegCore's GlobalFFOptions, and pushes the resolved paths into all three sub-services via new UpdateFFprobePath() / UpdateFFmpegPath() methods. Called at top of ProcessVideoAsync / ExtractSingleFrameAsync / ExtractSingleFrameWithFiltersAsync so scheduled tasks work even when the plugin boots before MediaEncoder. Verified live on Jellyfin 10.11.8 — scan task now extracts frames at 31% progress where previously it was 0/70 success. README header synced 1.6.1.14 → 1.6.1.16 (was missed in v1.6.1.15).

versions.changelog:
Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Adgangsnøglen: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende den på (X-Emby-Token). Det ramte Subtitle Guard hårdere end de andre plugins — tolv forskellige kald sendte den gamle vej, og de svarede alle 401 på Jellyfin 12. I praksis betød det at alt det der foregår fra selve siden holdt op med at virke: workers, køen, historikken, knapperne på detaljesiden. Alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt.

Indstillingssiden kunne slet ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Det er den side hvor workers tilmeldes, så uden den kunne en ny worker ikke sættes op. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på 2.1.0.0, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

Bemærk: selve sync-workeren er urørt. Den kører for sig selv og er ikke berørt af hvilken Jellyfin-version serveren har.

Undertekster der hører til en anden version af filmen bliver nu erstattet i stedet for at blive stående for evigt.

Baggrund: en rapporteret film (Superbad) havde undertekster der var så forkerte at man ikke kunne se om de kom for tidligt eller for sent. Filen er den uklippede udgave på 118,7 minutter, mens underteksten hører til biografudgaven og slutter 15 minutter før filmen gør. Indskudte scener fordeler sig ujævnt gennem filmen, så afvigelsen er ikke konstant - derfor kan man ikke pege på en retning.

Synkroniseringen var uskyldig. ffsubsync måler sammenhængen til -50.569 - altså negativ, modsat korreleret - og nægtede helt korrekt at røre filen. Til sammenligning gav seks afsnit med rigtige undertekster +40.205 til +177.137 og under 0,2 sekunds forskydning. Problemet var at intet i kæden så kunne redde filen: den ene reparation der virker - at transskribere lyden - var blokeret af netop den undertekst der var forkert. Filen kunne aldrig blive rigtig.

Workeren registrerer nu den slags som `subtitle-mismatch`, og en sådan undertekst tæller ikke længere som at elementet 'allerede har undertekster'. Den bliver transskriberet i stedet. Originalen gemmes som .bak inden den erstattes, hvis navnene støder sammen, så det altid kan fortrydes.

Bemærk: Whisper navngiver efter det sprog den finder (fx .en.srt), så en forkert undertekst der hedder .eng.srt bliver ikke overskrevet - den nye lægger sig ved siden af, og begge er synlige i afspilleren. Den forkerte kan slettes i hånden.

Kræver worker 2.3.0 eller nyere.

Manuelle klik (Fix undertekst-sync / Generér undertekster / Prøv igen) springer nu foran den natlige kø i stedet for at vente bag den - en natlig batch-kørsel kunne lægge hundredvis af filer foran et enkelt klik, så "Tilføjet til kø" reelt kunne betyde en lang ventetid. Bemærk: kræver genstart af Jellyfin for at tage effekt (denne del af rettelsen ligger i selve plugin'et, ikke i sync-workeren).

Selvdiagnosticerende advarsel hvis siden virker helt ustylet: en statisk boks øverst forklarer at File Transformation-pluginet formentlig mangler eller er inaktivt (det plugin der får Subtitle Guards egen kode til at køre) - synlig som ren HTML uden nogen afhængighed af JavaScript, og gemmes automatisk igen så snart pluginet faktisk kører korrekt. Ramte en ven der installerede pluginet og fik en helt ustylet side uden nogen forklaring; nu står årsagen der direkte i stedet.

Linux/Windows-vælger på 'Tilmeld ny worker': skift mellem Linux-kommandoen og den nye Windows-installer (PowerShell) - Windows GPU-maskiner (fx en gaming-pc) kan nu være workers med samme funktioner som Linux (sync, transskription, oversættelse). Workers males ikke længere 'Offline' under modelindlæsning: har workeren svaret inden for de sidste 3 minutter, vises seneste kendte status med en ⏳-note ('genstart ikke workeren') i stedet - vigtigt nu hvor workers frigiver hukommelsen efter endt arbejde og derfor genindlæser modeller ved hver natlig kørsel. Rettet: 'Seneste rettelser'-listen oversættes nu også i engelsk tilstand (den blev renderet før sprogvalget var indlæst).

Ny 'Test worker-rettigheder'-boks under Workers → Stier. Genererer en færdig kopiér-og-indsæt-kommando til check-permissions.sh, som tester ÆGTE læse/skrive/slette-rettigheder som den faktiske tjeneste-bruger på en worker (i modsætning til ls -l, der ofte lyver på netværks-mounts). Mappen udfyldes automatisk ud fra 'Inkluderede biblioteker' (med path mapping anvendt), men kan rettes til en hvilken som helst mappe. Ingen worker-opdatering nødvendig (scriptet hentes fra GitHub, når kommandoen køres).

Subtitle Guard 2.0 - feature-komplet udgave klar til at dele. NYT: engelsk UI (vælger øverst på siden - hele pluginet kan nu skifte mellem dansk og engelsk); 'Getting Started'-knap med fuld opsætningsguide (erstatter '?'); førstegangs-velkomst på Workers-fanen når ingen workers er tilmeldt; worker-version vises pr. maskine med markering af maskiner der halter efter poolen; 'Gendan originale undertekster' (alle workers gendanner ALT de har ændret, fra .bak-backupper - med er-du-sikker-bekræftelse); 'Gendan standardindstillinger'-knap (nulstiller alt undtagen worker-tilmelding, stier og sprog); Whisper-panelet forudfyldt med de anbefalede standarder. FORBEDRET: transskriptions-progressbaren animerer nu; Status-fanen opdaterer sig selv hvert minut, har fået en 'Tjek igen'-knap, og fejl forsvinder AUTOMATISK når et senere forsøg lykkes (viser nuværende tilstand, ikke historik); Pool-status-kortet er fjernet. RETTET (worker 2.0.0, ruller selv ud): 'Ryd kø' kunne miste kapløbet mod arbejdstrådene så jobs alligevel kørte - køen ryddes nu atomisk og bevarer pause-tilstanden; en pauset men ledig worker kunne stjæle nyindsendte jobs - de holdes nu i køen til der genoptages. Alt funktionelt testet mod en kørende worker-instans (21/21 checks, inkl. æøå gennem SRT-skriveren).

Indbygget opsætningsguide, CPU-transskription igen, og en Whisper-indstillings-UI. Et nyt '?' i toppen af plugin-siden åbner en fuld trin-for-trin guide til at sætte workers op - med et fremhævet afsnit om at worker-kontoen SKAL have skriverettigheder til medierne (ellers fejler alt med 'permission denied'), inkl. SERVICE_USER og gruppe-fix. CPU-workers kan nu transskribere igen: routingen er ikke længere CUDA-only, men styres af transskriptions-rollen - Workers-listen advarer om at CPU giver lavere kvalitet og anbefaler GPU. Ny sektion under Transskription: Whisper-indstillinger (model, beam size, VAD + tærskel/padding) med en forklaring til hver, som genererer en færdig kopier-og-indsæt-kommando du kører på den ønskede worker (indstillingerne sidder pr. worker, så de gemmes ikke i pluginet). Desuden en ny 'Aktivér dansk oversættelse'-kontakt, så hele oversættelsesfunktionen kan slås fra. Nye CPU-workers vælger nu selv Whisper-model ud fra kerner/RAM ved installation (small, eller medium på ≥4 kerner og ≥6 GB RAM; large-v3 er GPU-only i auto-valget, men kan stadig vælges manuelt). Selve pluginet kræver ingen worker-opdatering; auto-modelvalget gælder ved (gen)installation af en worker.

Fejl-triage, historik-forbedringer, kvalitetspas, live fremdrift, auto-oversættelse og multi-GPU. Status-fanen får et rødt triage-kort der grupperer fejl efter årsag (skriverettigheder, manglende mount, model-cache osv.) med konkrete løsningsforslag og en 'Prøv fejlede igen nu'-knap der sætter alle tre opgaver i kø. Transskriptions-historikken viser nu seneste status PR. EMNE (gamle fejl forsvinder når et nyt forsøg lykkes) og fejlede rækker får en 'Prøv igen'-knap. Whisper-output renses for hallucinationer (thanks-for-watching/subtitles-by-boilerplate og gentagelses-loops). Emne-sidens 'Generér undertekster'-knap viser nu live fremdrift ('Transskriberer... 42%' -> 'Færdig'). Ny indstilling: automatisk en->da-oversættelse i kø straks efter en vellykket engelsk transskription (til som standard). Installeren understøtter nu flere instanser pr. maskine (INSTALL_DIR/SERVICE_NAME/WORKER_PORT/GPU_INDEX), så fx en 3080 + 2060 kører som to uafhængige workers. Worker-delen ruller selv ud via auto-opdateringen.

Metadata-hotwords til Whisper. Før hver transskription bygges automatisk en kort, rangeret liste af navne og særegne termer fra emnets Jellyfin-metadata - serie-/film-/afsnitstitler, karakternavne, skuespillere, tags/collections og egennavne udtrukket lokalt fra resuméer (afsnit kombineres med serie-metadata) - og gives til faster-whisper's hotwords, så 'Chrisjen Avasarala' staves rigtigt i stedet for fonetisk gætværk. Dubletter fjernes (mest specifikke form vinder), apostroffer/bindestreger/accenter bevares, og listen er begrænset (75 termer / 800 tegn, konfigurerbart). Nye indstillinger under Transskription: aktivér (til), maks. termer/tegn, skuespillere (til), instruktører/forfattere (fra), resuméer (til), studier (fra), debug-log (fra - normalt logges kun antallet). Cachet pr. emne og ugyldiggjort ved metadata-ændringer; intet metadata forlader serveren. Worker-delen ruller selv ud via auto-opdateringen. Bemærk: hotwords er en bias, ikke en garanti - de øger sandsynligheden for korrekte stavemåder markant.

Blåt tema, undertekst-boks/skygge og sprogfilter på emne-sider. Plugin-siden er farvelagt om fra violet til et moderne blåt tema (grafen bruger nu teal til Oversat så de to blå ikke flyder sammen), og CC-logoet i toppen er fjernet. To nye undertekst-indstillinger under Udseende: Baggrundsboks (0-100% sort boks bag teksten, 60-70 giver det klassiske TV-look) og Skygge (0-4 blød slagskygge, kan kombineres med kantlinjen) - begge dækker begge render-stier. Undertekst-vælgeren på emne-sider (detail-siden) respekterer nu listen over synlige sprog: ét spor pr. sprog (ikke-SDH foretrækkes), utaggede spor beholdes, og det aktuelt valgte spor fjernes aldrig. Ingen worker-opdatering nødvendig.

Config-page overhaul, transcription history, stats & graphs, new status glyphs (Phase C). The plugin page is rebuilt around a hero header, card layout, icon tabs and built-in guides (how sync works, step-by-step worker enrollment with a copyable install-kommando, CPU/GPU role guidance). Transskription tab gains a pool-wide transcription history (outcome, sprog-chip, tidspunkt, worker). Status tab opens with stat tiles (Rettet/I sync/Transskriberet/Oversat/Fejlet) and a stacked 14-dages aktivitetsgraf med hover-tooltips. Worker-status glyffer er nu animerede: åndende grøn med ring (ledig), roterende violet bue (arbejder), gule bjælker (pauset), pulserende rød (offline). KRÆVER worker-opdatering på alle maskiner (nye /stats- og /history-endpoints ligger i workeren).

Worker roles, true sync+ML concurrency, and transcription progress (Phase B). Roles: every worker now carries which jobs it may do (Synkronisering/Transskription/Oversættelse) - set via checkboxes at enrollment and editable afterwards as clickable chips on the worker list; routing requires the role AND the advertised capability (existing workers default to all roles). Concurrency: the worker now runs two queues - sync threads keep flowing while ONE dedicated ML thread handles transcriptions/translations, fixing a starvation bug where queued transcriptions could block every sync thread; a both-roles box genuinely syncs and transcribes at once. Progress: transcriptions report a real percentage (segment position vs media duration), painted as a 5-block bar with % on the worker list. REQUIRES a worker update on all machines (two queues + progress live in the worker script).

iOS Safari subtitle fix (Phase A). iOS hands fullscreen playback to Apple's native player, which ignores Jellyfin's HTML subtitle overlay - so text subtitles vanish in fullscreen on iPhone/iPad. The plugin now fixes this by burning the selected subtitle into the video, but ONLY on iOS: on an iOS/iPadOS device it rewrites the PlaybackInfo device profile so text subs are delivered as Encode (burn-in), per-playback, with no persistent setting changed. Desktop and TV are untouched and keep the styled overlay (no extra transcode). Toggle under Undertekster: 'Indbrænd undertekster på iOS' (default on). Note: iOS playback with a subtitle now transcodes, which is the cost of guaranteed fullscreen subtitles there.

Subtitle styling (Phase A): standardized appearance now covers font family and a configurable black outline/border (0-4px), on top of size. Size is computed live from the ACTIVE PLAYER's rendered height and re-applied on resize/fullscreen/orientation/playback-start, so it scales with the player (not just the window) on desktop, mobile and TV-web - with a viewport clamp as the pre-player fallback. Both render paths are covered (the browser's native ::cue renderer and Jellyfin's HTML overlay). New settings under Undertekster: Skrifttype and Kantlinje (px). More Phase A items (media-page language enforcement, iOS Safari) to follow.

Transcription is now CUDA-only with no CPU fallback: when the GPU worker is offline, transcribe jobs simply aren't queued anywhere, rather than silently falling back to a CPU worker's less accurate 'small' model as before. Also fixes the detail-page 'Fix undertekst-sync'/'Generér undertekster' buttons, whose label text had no CSS of its own and inherited an oversized default font-size - it widened the button row enough to crowd the logo/release-date at narrower window widths. Labels are now sized to match the rest of the UI and collapse to icon-only (tooltip retained) below 1000px. Carries forward the per-item transcribe button now sending force:true, so re-transcribing an item overwrites its previous output (v1.4.2.0, never released standalone).

Stability fixes (no new features). Transcription/translation were failing on every job because the v1.4.0.0 installer never gave the service user a writable model cache - each job re-downloaded the model from HuggingFace and hit a 429 rate limit. The installer now sets a fixed HF_HOME in the install dir and pre-downloads the Whisper model + NLLB tokenizer during install (with retry), so runtime never contacts HuggingFace; re-run the installer on each worker to apply. Added an ffsubsync sanity clamp: results with an implausibly large offset (>60s, SUBWORKER_MAX_OFFSET) are rejected and the original kept, preventing 'way off' corruptions (shown as 'sprunget over' in the pool summary). Note: 'Permission denied' sync failures are a filesystem-permissions issue (give the worker's service user write access to those media folders).

The big overhaul. Seneste rettelser rollback menu (last 5 rewritten subs with offset/time/worker and one-click Fortryd rettelse restoring the .bak - rollbacks are remembered so the nightly task won't undo them). Library scoping via 'Included libraries' (e.g. /Media/Movies,/Media/Shows - Standup/Western stay untouched). Danish translation: NLLB-200 distilled-1.3B on GPU workers translates English subs (external or embedded, ffmpeg-extracted) to .da.srt with original timings, nightly at 02:00. Subtitle-menu cleanup: hides non-da/en tracks, SDH/CC variants, and duplicate languages in the player - one clean choice per language. Live per-job activity per worker (Synkroniserer/Transskriberer/Oversætter: <navn>). New indicators: glowing green idle, spinning ring working, pause bars, red offline. Settings reorganized into tabs. Work stealing: idle workers pull from the deepest peer queue (capability-aware). Pool totals in Status tab; pause survives worker reboots. Update workers with the installer one-liner (GPU machine downloads the NLLB model once, ~6GB; enrollment codes preserved).

Sync throughput + pool coordination + controls. Parallel sync: workers run several jobs at once (default min(4, cores-1); transcriptions stay one-at-a-time for GPU memory) - tune with SUBWORKER_SYNC_CONCURRENCY, which doubles as a bandwidth cap since each job streams a full media file. Pool-wide dedupe: the plugin merges every worker's completed-work ledger before distributing, so a freshly-enrolled worker no longer redoes files others already finished (mtime-verified, so re-downloaded subs still get redone). Per-worker Pause/Fortsæt and Ryd kø buttons in settings; paused workers show grey with waiting count; multi-file activity display. Update each worker with the usual installer one-liner (enrollment codes preserved).

Whisper transcription (Phase B). Workers can now generate subtitles: they advertise a transcription capability (CUDA large-v3 or CPU small, auto-detected - re-run the installer on each worker to add Whisper support; it now keeps the existing enrollment code). New scheduled task 'Generate missing subtitles' (default 01:00) queues every item without a text subtitle in the target languages (default da,en) - jobs go only to Whisper-capable workers, exclusively to GPU workers when one is online, and the run skips gracefully when none are up. 'Generér undertekster' button on item pages. Output written as <name>.<lang>.srt next to the media; existing subtitle files are never overwritten. Worker list shows each machine's Whisper capability. Limitation: Whisper transcribes the spoken language (English movies get English subs); Danish translation is a possible future phase.

Fix: the plugin frontend could crash at page load and take everything with it - subtitle sizing, the rendering watchdog, and the settings-page wiring ('Tilføj worker' did nothing). Root cause: the script asked for window.ApiClient before Jellyfin's bootstrap had created it; losing that race threw an error that prevented the plugin's page-watcher from ever being installed. Everything now waits for ApiClient readiness and the watcher installs unconditionally and crash-proof, so the settings page wires itself reliably on every load.

Fix: 'Tilføj worker' could do nothing after updating - the browser paired a stale cached copy of the previous version's script with the new settings page, so the button never got its click handler. The injected script URL now carries the plugin version (guaranteed cache miss on every update; no hard refresh needed anymore). Worker list: pulsing amber dot with 'arbejder på: <file>' while a worker processes, done/failed counters, and statuses auto-refresh every 10s while the settings page is open.

Multi-worker pool. Enroll any number of machines with the one-line curl installer (each prints its URL + enrollment code, pasted into the new worker list in settings, which shows live online/offline status and queue depth per worker with add/remove management). The nightly task and per-item button split jobs between whichever workers are online - powered-off machines are skipped. Files are consistently assigned to the same worker (stable path hash) so each machine's already-checked database stays effective; offline machines' work is deterministically picked up by the others. v1.1.0.0 single-worker settings migrate automatically. This pool is the foundation for the upcoming Whisper transcription phase.

Subtitle sync fixer. New companion worker service (worker/subtitle-worker in the repo, one-script install on any Debian/Ubuntu machine with file access to the media) aligns drifted external subtitles to the audio via ffsubsync - only files off by more than 0.4s are touched, originals kept as .bak, checked file versions remembered so repeated runs are cheap. Plugin: 'Fix subtitle sync' scheduled task (default daily 04:00) submits the whole library nightly; 'Fix undertekst-sync' button on item pages for on-demand fixes; settings for worker URL, API key, and path mapping.

First release. Standardized viewport-scaled subtitle size for both rendering paths (video::cue native cues and the .videoSubtitles HTML overlay), configurable 50-200%. Rendering watchdog: while a video plays with a text subtitle selected, verifies every 8s that a showing text track with loaded cues (or the HTML overlay) exists, and re-applies the subtitle selection via SetSubtitleStreamIndex (off, then back on) when it silently fails - a real failure mode reproduced live. 20s startup grace, max two fix attempts per item, burned-in/image subtitles skipped.

Afspil-knappen følger temaets egne farver - på ElegantFin lysegrå med sort tekst - i stedet for Jellyfins blå, også mens temaet indlæses.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden hentes meget hurtigere.

- Alle otte baggrunde blev hentet på én gang i 1920 gange skærmens pixeltæthed - 2880 px på en almindelig bærbar og 3,5 MB, mens forsiden stadig var ved at indlæse. Nu hentes kun det slide, der vises, og det næste, i en størrelse der passer til skærmen.
- Logoerne hentes også først, når deres slide er på vej.
- Indtil baggrunden er hentet, vises en sløret udgave af den.
- Størrelserne er dem, New Badges 2.8.2.0 laver på forhånd på serveren, så billederne kommer med det samme.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Intet blink i topbaren, når du scroller helt op.

- Når siden ramte toppen, skiftede Jellyfin 12 topbarens udseende og fjernede samtidig den markering, der gør den gennemsigtig over banneret. I et splitsekund kom temaets farvede bar frem og forsvandt igen. Markeringen sidder nu et sted, Jellyfin ikke rører, så topbaren forbliver gennemsigtig.
- Topbaren bliver nu gennemsigtig med det samme i stedet for at tone ud, så temaets farve ikke hænger et øjeblik i toppen, når du hopper helt op.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Mindre prikker på mobil og tablet.

- Prikkerne, der viser hvilket slide du er på, fyldte omkring halvdelen af skærmbredden på en telefon. De er nu mindre og tættere.
- Den aktive prik blev tegnet i hele sit trykfelt og var derfor en stor hvid plet. Den er nu kun lidt større end de andre.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Ingen streg under den gennemsigtige topbar.

- Skyggen, der holder topbarens knapper læsbare over banneret, sad på selve topbaren og stoppede ved dens underkant, så den tegnede omridset af den gamle topbar. Den ligger nu på banneret og toner blødt ud et godt stykke længere nede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Gennemsigtig topbar over banneret på Jellyfin 12.

- Banneret går helt op under topbaren, og topbaren er gennemsigtig, så billedet fylder hele toppen af forsiden.
- Når du scroller forbi banneret, bliver topbaren almindelig igen.
- På Favoritter, Tilføj, Kalender og alle andre sider er topbaren som før.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Banneret husker sine slides mellem besøg - de skifter alligevel kun hver 48. time - så det vises med det samme, når du åbner appen. Før blev 400 titler hentet igen ved hvert besøg, mens Jellyfins egne rækker ventede.
- Når der skal vælges nye slides, hentes kun id'erne på de 400 kandidater og derefter de 8 valgte, i stedet for alle detaljer om alle 400.
- Afspil/Fortsæt og favorit-hjertet opdateres, når Jellyfins egne rækker er indlæst, så banneret ikke sinker dem.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Retter at pluginets indstillingsside ikke kunne åbnes på Jellyfin 12.

Pluginet kørte fint, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun en plugin-indstillingsside, hvis siden selv beder om at komme i menuen. Det gør den nu.

Kun relevant for Jellyfin 12 — på 10.11 kunne siden altid åbnes fra plugin-oversigten uanset hvad.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12. Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan KUN installeres der - Jellyfin 10.11 bliver på 2.0.4.0, som stadig virker uændret. Serveren vælger selv den rigtige.

Hvad der skulle laves om: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt i stedet. Uden det svarede serveren 401, og heroens "mest sete"-data kunne ikke hentes.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven - men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en helt ny måde, hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve. Jellyfin 12 udstiller hele sin farvepalet direkte, så nu bliver den bare spurgt. På 10.11 fungerer den gamle metode som før.

Rettet: Afspil/Fortsæt-knappen i hero-baren skiftede af og til til Jellyfins standardblå i stedet for temaets egen grå. Pluginet aflæser temaets accentfarve fra siden, og hvis den aflæsning sker før temaets stylesheet er nået at blive indlæst – på denne server hentes skinnet via et @import fra et CDN – aflæses browserens standardfarve i stedet, og så faldt knappen tilbage til blå. Farven blev kun genberegnet ved DOM-ændringer (højst hvert 10. sekund), så på en side der lå stille kunne den blive blå indtil næste genindlæsning. Nu huskes den sidst korrekt aflæste farve, så en mislykket aflæsning aldrig kan overskrive en god, og farven genberegnes desuden et par gange kort efter sideindlæsning og igen ved "load".

Mindre mørklægning af billedet i hero-baren. Toningen bag titel og knapper er sat ned til 70% af det oprindelige, og ind-/udtoningen i top og bund er trukket ind (18%/78% → 10%/86%), så en større del af plakaten er synlig. Styrken kan nu justeres i indstillingerne ("Artwork tint strength") mellem 0 og 150% – teksten har sin egen skygge, så den kan læses et godt stykke under 100.

Hero-baren kan nu vise et tilfældigt udvalg fra hele biblioteket i stedet for "trending + senest tilføjet" - og udvalget er det SAMME for alle brugere på serveren. Det skiftes automatisk ud hver 48. time (kan ændres i indstillingerne). Udvalget trækkes ikke tilfældigt pr. bruger eller pr. sideindlæsning - det udledes af uret, så alle lander på præcis de samme titler uden at serveren skal gemme noget, og det skifter helt af sig selv når vinduet ruller over (justeret efter UTC, så det sker samtidigt for alle). Kan slås fra igen i indstillingerne.

Rettelse på mobil: slide-prikkerne lå oven i knapperne. Prikkerne sad nederst til højre - samme linje som Afspil/Info/Favorit-rækken - og blev tegnet ovenpå den. Målt live på en 360px skærm med dansk knaptekst (Fortsæt i stedet for Afspil) overlappede de to 112 pixels, så prikkerne løb tværs hen over Info- og favoritknappen. Det er et pladsproblem, som først opstår omkring 470px, og derfor kun ses på telefon: knapraden mod otte berøringsvenlige prikker klemt op i højre side. På skærme under 500px flytter prikkerne nu op i øverste højre hjørne - fri plads i alle slides, eftersom motivet ligger i midten/til højre og teksten nederst til venstre, og netop dér en karrusel normalt viser sin position på mobil.

Bygget til at kunne deles. Farvetonen hen over billedet og knapperne henter nu deres farver fra det tema du kører, i stedet for at være håndmatchet til ét bestemt skin, så heroen glider ind i et hvilket som helst tema - også de lyse. Knapteksterne følger Jellyfins egen sprogindstilling (dansk/engelsk, eller tvunget). Nye indstillinger: sprog, højde, om synopsis og favoritknappen skal vises, og hvor langt tilbage trending kigger.

Ens knapform i alle vinduesstørrelser. Info/Afspil/Favorit-knapperne har nu præcis samme facon i fuldskærm, halvt vindue og på mobil: fast min-højde + border-box ligger i grundreglen, og media queries ændrer ikke længere padding/højde (det var dem der gjorde knapperne synligt anderledes ved smallere bredder).

Fixes the Info button looking visibly 'fluffier' than the Play/Favorite buttons next to it: Info is an <a> element while the other two are real <button>s, and without an explicit reset each rendered with its own element's default font/appearance despite sharing the same CSS class. Added a font-family/line-height/appearance reset to the shared button style so all three render pixel-consistent.

Mobile + performance: touch swipe changes hero slides, with touch events contained inside the hero so Jellyfin's tab strip no longer hijacks a hero swipe into a tab switch (the swipe-to-Favoritter bug); vertical scrolling unaffected. Manual slide changes (dots, swipes) share the rotation's slide counter and restart its timer, fixing desynced auto-flips. Tailored phone layout: shorter banner, tighter text/logo sizing, tappable 40px buttons, larger dot hit areas. Performance: recently-added/trending pool cached 10 min in sessionStorage so the hero paints instantly on revisit; resume/next-up state always fetched fresh.

Visual: the hero now blends into the page background instead of ending in a hard box edge. The backdrop and tint layers sit behind a vertical alpha mask that fades them out at the top and bottom, letting ElegantFin's real background gradient (measured live: linear-gradient(0deg, rgb(28,30,34) 35%, rgb(37,39,45))) show through - a true blend with no color matching involved. Text, buttons, and pagination dots are outside the masked layer and stay fully crisp.

Fix: v1.0.0.0 could stack many duplicate heroes on the home page - the duplicate check ran synchronously but insertion happened after async data fetches, so every DOM mutation during that window started another insert; now guarded by a synchronously-set pending flag plus a re-check right before insertion. Play button now actually starts playback (remote-controls the client's own session via the Sessions PlayNow command) instead of linking to the details page, with details as fallback if the play command fails. Dynamic play button: shows Fortsæt and resumes where you left off for partially-watched movies, and for series in progress plays the half-watched episode (Resume) or the next unwatched episode (NextUp).

Initial release. Recently added + trending item mix (trending via the same Playback Reporting query New Badges' Trending row uses), ClearLogo image per slide with automatic text-title fallback when no logo art exists, rating/year/age-rating/genre metadata line, truncated overview, Play/Info/Favorite buttons, clickable pagination dots, and configurable slide count/rotation interval/trending toggle. Built as an in-flow first child of #homeTab (not a body-level overlay like Media Bar), so it never overlaps Mine medier/Continue Watching and needs no manual positioning fixes. Uses the verified ElegantFin header color (rgba(30,40,54,...)) for its gradient overlay so it blends into the header with no seam at any window width.
